subject: GreenPlay evaluation: scope clarifications, hyperscaler comparison & proposed tests
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@greenplay.com>, Michael O'Neill <m.oneill@greenplay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: GreenPlay evaluation: scope clarifications, hyperscaler comparison & proposed tests

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciated the candid feedback. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and what we'll deliver for a clean comparison vs the hyperscalers:

Recap (what we showed)
- Live demo of Redwood hosted API and Dedicated routing policies (cost/latency lanes)
- Private deployment options (VPC in-region, audit logs, KMS integration)
- Streaming + continuous batching behavior that reduces p50 latency for short-turn chat

You said your top priorities were: EU latency (p99 targets for chat), strict EU data residency, and an apples-to-apples cost/quality comparison vs Bedrock/Vertex. To be concrete, here are the tests we propose (attached spreadsheet with details):

Proposed test plan (high level)
1) Regional latency sweep (EU): p50/p95/p99 across eu-west-1 (Dublin), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), and a baseline US region. Measure both cold-start and warmed cache behavior.
2) Burst throughput: 1k concurrent short-chat sessions (simulated Black Friday peak) to validate autoscaling and tail latency under load.
3) Quality parity: run 3 GreenPlay prompt sets (product search, returns handling, and conversational checkout) through Redwood + Bedrock + Vertex and compare accuracy, hallucination rate, and time-to-first-token.
4) Compliance & log residency check: confirm that audit logs, KV cache, and any temporary request metadata remain in the EU when using Private (VPC) deployment.

What we need from you to proceed
- A short prioritized wishlist (latency vs cost vs functionality) — single-line bullets are fine.
- Example prompt files (I attached a starter set 'benchmark-sample-prompts.txt') and a target SLA for p99 latency if you have one.
- Permission to run Bedrock and Vertex comparisons with the sample prompts (we can redact PII) — if GreenPlay wants to run the hyperscaler side, we can take data formats and run them on our end for parity.

Tentative timeline
- Kickoff and dataset handoff: Mon 2027-05-24
- Latency & quality runs: 2027-05-25 — 2027-05-28
- Deliver results & cost estimates: 2027-06-01

Attachments: GreenPlay_MVP_test_plan.xlsx, redwood-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf, benchmark-sample-prompts.txt

If that all looks good, I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next Tuesday to lock down test ownership and access.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

--

From: Elena Ramos <elena@greenplay.com>

Cc: Michael O'Neill <m.oneill@greenplay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 19:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: GreenPlay evaluation: scope clarifications, hyperscaler comparison & proposed tests

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the proposed plan:

Priorities (short list)
- Data residency: must stay in the EU for both model execution and audit logs (GDPR + internal policy).
- Latency: our internal goal is p99 < 180ms for short-turn chat (messages < 32 tokens) across our EU edge points.
- Cost visibility: we want a line-item cost estimate for the three modes (hosted, dedicated reserved, private) with assumptions called out.

Questions / constraints
- Can Redwood deploy a Private control plane or Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 with logs permanently retained in the EU?
- For the hyperscaler comparisons, will you run Bedrock/Vertex from their respective EU regions or do you expect GreenPlay to provide accounts?
- SOC2 + audit evidence: we need to confirm what artifacts Redwood can provide (scope, retention, map of logs to EU storage).

Michael and I also want to include a short sample of production traffic (syntheticized if needed) — I can share a redacted dataset by EOD Monday.

If you can confirm the answers above, we'll prioritize the test sets and confirm Tuesday availability.

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering | GreenPlay Retail
elena@greenplay.com | +44 20 7946 0123
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@greenplay.com>, Michael O'Neill <m.oneill@greenplay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenPlay evaluation: scope clarifications, hyperscaler comparison & proposed tests

Great questions — quick answers below and then an updated action plan at the end.

Answers
- Private deployment & logs in EU: yes. We offer Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane that can be provisioned in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1. Audit logs and KV cache can be configured to land in EU-only storage (we'll show the KMS/HSM integration during the run).
- Hyperscaler side-by-side: we can run the Redwood side from our EU hosts. For Bedrock/Vertex, we can either run using our internal eval accounts (if OK) or you can provide scoped read-only accounts for GreenPlay — both approaches are fine, we just need credentials or permission to run. We'll document the region used for each run.
- SOC2 artifacts: we can provide the SOC2 scope summary and mapping of evidence; for controlled artifacts that require NDA or an enterprise agreement we can pick the right channel.

Updated action plan
1) You share redacted sample traffic by EOD Mon (we'll accept S3 link or Drive).
2) Marissa and Logan will run a regional latency sweep (DUB/FRA/us) and a short quality pass on the three prompt sets.
3) We'll produce a cost/latency matrix and a small write-up mapping how Redwood's routing and batching affects the p99 outcome vs the hyperscalers.

I'll put together an invite for Tue 2027-05-25 to confirm dataset handoff and who will run the hyperscaler side.

Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: GreenPlay next-tests coordination (latency + hyperscaler runs)

Folks — forwarding Elena's notes. High level split below. Please ack and paste any blockers.

Marissa (you): lead the latency sweep and quality pass. Deliverable: CSV with p50/p95/p99 per-region (DUB, FRA, US) and a short notes column for cache-warm vs cold. Target: 2027-05-28 EOD.
Logan (you): provision Dedicated pool / Private control plane in eu-west-1 for the runs. Ensure KMS/EU storage config (retention window = 90 days for audit logs).
Lauren (you): prepare three pricing options (hosted blended, 6-month reserved dedicated, private deployment + support) with assumptions. We need ballpark estimates ready for the 6/1 deliverable.

Risks we should call out in the report
- Hyperscaler region parity: Bedrock+Vertex may have slightly different instance types that affect tail latency; we'll clearly flag any hardware mismatches.
- Dataset representativeness: Elena will share redacted production samples — we should include a note on how synthetic vs real traffic might change p99.

Please confirm by EOD so I can lock the kickoff with GreenPlay for Mon.

— Ben (on behalf of GreenPlay opportunity)
